title: Improving Student Accounts and Collections in Higher Education
summary: Learn how colleges can strengthen student accounts and collections with better reporting, oversight, and capacity to recover more revenue.
body_text: For colleges and universities, student accounts and collections are no longer just back-office functions. Instead, they are part of a broader financial operations strategy that affects cash flow, liquidity, student experience, staffing capacity, vendor oversight, and institutional decision-making. That strategic importance is underscored by the size of outstanding balances many institutions are managing. A recent survey of more than 150 higher education leaders by ECSI and Higher Ed Dive found that about seven in 10 institutions reported past-due tuition and fee receivables portfolios of $1 million or more, with a meaningful share managing more than $5 million in outstanding balances. At that level, the issue extends beyond payment processing or account recovery. Business officers need confidence that staffing structures, technology tools, and third-party relationships provide the insight and flexibility required to support long-term institutional goals. Student Financial Operations Face Growing Demands Student accounts teams are responsible for a range of critical functions, including billing, payment processing, collections, account reconciliation, and reporting. These responsibilities directly affect both institutional cash flow and the student experience. At the same time, turnover, hiring challenges, and competing priorities can make it difficult to maintain consistent processes while responding to requests from leadership, students, and other departments. As a result, finance teams are often being asked to deliver more insight and accountability with the same — or fewer — resources. Business officers increasingly need answers to questions such as: How effective are current collections efforts? Are third-party collection agencies performing as expected? Where do bottlenecks exist within billing or payment processes? Which operational activities consume the most staff time? What information is needed to support financial planning and decision-making? Providing timely answers can be challenging when data is spread across multiple systems or departments. Rethinking Collections Strategies Collections remain an important component of many institutions’ financial operations, but the way collections are managed continues to evolve. Some institutions rely primarily on internal staff, while others utilize third-party collection agencies or hybrid approaches. Regardless of the model, leaders are increasingly focused on evaluating performance and ensuring resources are directed toward activities that deliver the greatest value. That evaluation often includes questions about: Vendor effectiveness Recovery performance Reporting transparency Student communication practices Internal oversight and accountability As collection activities become more distributed across internal teams and external partners, leaders need a clear view of what is working and where adjustments may be needed. Higher education leaders are looking beyond traditional recovery metrics and seeking a more comprehensive understanding of how collections activities impact operational efficiency, financial outcomes, and the student experience. Visibility Drives Better Decisions One of the most common challenges institutions face is limited visibility into student accounts and collections activity. Information may exist within multiple systems, reports, or departments, making it difficult to develop a clear picture of performance. Staff often spend significant time gathering data, reconciling information, and preparing reports for leadership. Improved reporting and analytics can help institutions: Monitor outstanding balances more effectively Identify emerging collection trends Evaluate agency performance Improve forecasting accuracy Support stronger decision-making When leaders have access to timely, reliable information, they are often better positioned to allocate resources, identify process improvement opportunities, and respond to changing financial conditions. Addressing Staffing and Capacity Constraints Staffing challenges remain a significant concern across higher education. Many student financial operations teams are being asked to manage growing workloads while maintaining service levels and supporting increasingly complex reporting requirements. In some cases, highly skilled staff members spend valuable time performing administrative or repetitive tasks that limit their ability to focus on higher-value activities. Collections work can be a particularly resource-intensive example of that strain. In the same ECSI and Higher Ed Dive survey, about 74% of higher education officers indicated their teams spend 10% to 24% of their time attempting to recover delinquent tuition and fees. Reducing that administrative burden often requires a combination of strategies, including process standardization, workflow improvements, automation opportunities, and supplemental support models that expand operational capacity without requiring additional full-time hires. The objective is not simply to do more with fewer people. Rather, it is to ensure that finance professionals can focus their expertise where it has the greatest impact. Building a Stronger Operating Model Improving student accounts and collections performance often begins with understanding how people, processes, technology, and vendors interact across the entire lifecycle. Institutions that take a holistic approach may identify opportunities to: Streamline billing and collection workflows Improve coordination between departments Strengthen oversight of third-party providers Reduce administrative inefficiencies Small improvements across multiple areas can collectively create meaningful gains in efficiency, accountability, and financial performance. Depending on the institution’s needs, this work may include redesigning accounting and allocation processes, supporting complex multi-entity or grant environments, transitioning from Excel-based tracking to purpose-built systems, validating reporting methodologies, or developing automated dashboards for leadership. The goal is to create a more consistent, transparent, and scalable foundation for student financial operations. Looking Ahead As colleges and universities navigate continued pressure on resources and margins, strengthening student accounts and collections can help leaders improve recovery outcomes, use staff capacity more effectively, and make more informed decisions. Unlocking the Grid: A Deep Dive into Tesla FSD v14.3.5 and the Revolutionary Active Camera Preview Feature

body_text: Introduction On Monday, July 13, 2026, Tesla officially initiated the rollout of its highly anticipated Over-the-Air (OTA) software update, version 2026.20.6.6, carrying the internal neural network designation of Full Self-Driving (FSD) v14.3.5. While point releases in Tesla’s operating system framework often serve as minor bug-fix compilations, this specific deployment marks a monumental shift in how the vehicle shares visual perception telemetry with its human operator. For years, the camera feeds processing Tesla’s advanced spatial neural networks have remained a “black box” to the average driver. FSD visualizes the world as a synthetic vector space—bounding boxes, localized lanes, and kinetic path predictions rendered on the central touchscreen. While mathematically impressive, this abstraction layer often detached the driver from the raw optical realities perceived by the car's physical CMOS sensors. With FSD v14.3.5, Tesla introduces a major feature update: Active Camera Preview . For the first time in Tesla's history, owners can monitor, view, and isolate every single external and internal camera stream in real-time, even while the vehicle is cruising autonomously on highways or complex urban arterials. This analytical deep dive unpacks the architectural mechanics of this new software upgrade, explores its foundational hardware constraints across Hardware 3 (HW3) and Hardware 4 (HW4) systems, and provides practical insights for modern EV owners. II. Technical Breakdown of FSD v14.3.5 & Active Camera Preview To understand the significance of this software release, one must first explore the system's digital pathways. Previously, the "Camera Preview" application, which displays a consolidated visual grid of the car’s cameras, was strictly gated by safety interlocks. It could only be accessed when the transmission was set to "Park". If the driver shifted into "Drive" or "Reverse," the system immediately terminated the multi-view application, defaulting to the standard visualizer and the single, mandatory rear-facing backup camera. Under the architecture of FSD v14.3.5, this safety lock has been completely re-engineered. Drivers can access the system at any time by navigating to: Controls > Service > Camera Preview The Nine-Box Spatial Grid Upon activation, the central processor renders a high-definition 9-box grid overlay on the right-hand quadrant of the display. This grid populates in real-time with zero noticeable frame-rate lag, pulling directly from the vehicle’s physical camera array: Camera Position Sensor Type Field of View (FoV) Primary Autonomous Function Front Main Camera Triple-Lens System (HW3) / Dual-Lens (HW4) 120° Horizontal Long-range pathing, highway object detection Front Wide Camera Wide-Angle Lens 150° Horizontal Intersection crossing, close-quarters obstacle detection Front Bumper Camera Ultra-Wide Macro (2025+ Model Y / Cybertruck) 180° Horizontal Eliminates front blind-spots, low-height curb detection Left Side Repeater Fender-mounted Rearward Facing 80° Diagonal Blind-spot monitoring, highway lane merges Right Side Repeater Fender-mounted Rearward Facing 80° Diagonal Blind-spot monitoring, highway lane merges Left B-Pillar Camera Door-pillar Forward Facing 90° Diagonal Cross-traffic analysis, unprotected left turns Right B-Pillar Camera Door-pillar Forward Facing 90° Diagonal Cross-traffic analysis, unprotected left turns Rear-View Camera Liftgate-mounted 140° Wide Angle Reversing, rear-end hazard mitigation Interior Cabin Camera Rearview-mirror integrated Wide Infrared Driver monitoring, occupant safety, cabin security Individual Expansion Logic The UI allows the driver to tap on any of these nine active thumbnail feeds. Doing so instantly scales that specific stream to a larger, dedicated viewing block while maintaining a minimized grid of the remaining eight feeds along the margins. Tapping a dedicated "Grid" button instantly snaps the display back to the uniform, multi-stream configuration. Underlying Network Compiler Upgrades (MLIR & C++) What makes active previews technologically viable without degrading FSD path-planning latency is a ground-up rewrite of Tesla’s internal compiler. Previously, rendering video feeds was processed sequentially through standard graphics pipelines, which risked memory-bandwidth starvation when the main FSD neural network was executing at 36 Hz (36 frames of prediction per second). By implementing an MLIR (Multi-Level Intermediate Representation) compiler framework , Tesla's software division has decoupled the vision-perception pipeline from the visual-display pipeline. FSD v14.3.5 enjoys a 20% acceleration in core model reaction times because the compiler now prioritizes inference compute kernels over standard UI rendering operations. In simpler terms, your Tesla can now paint a high-fidelity 9-stream video on your screen without sacrificing a single millisecond of its autonomous braking, steering, or decision-making capabilities. III. Hardware Compatibility: HW4 vs. Legacy HW3 (FSD v14 Lite) While the active camera preview operates flawlessly on HW4-equipped vehicles (possessing superior central processing units, dedicated graphics buses, and higher-megapixel cameras), legacy Hardware 3 (HW3) owners face a different architectural reality. The HW3 Bandwidth Bottleneck Vehicles equipped with HW3 run on a platform engineered in 2018. While incredibly capable, the SoC (System on Chip) features significantly lower memory bandwidth and a much tighter thermal envelope. Because FSD v14 introduces complex, deeply parameter-rich vision models, HW3 cannot natively process the full, uncompressed weights of the network. To resolve this, Tesla developed FSD v14 Lite specifically for HW3 cars. This "Lite" version utilizes INT8 quantization and selective weight pruning to match the functional output of HW4 networks without triggering system-wide memory overflows. Active Preview Constraints on HW3 When an HW3-equipped Tesla Model 3 or Model Y activates Active Camera Preview during autonomous driving, the system dynamically scales down the preview frame rates: HW4 Vehicles: All 8 or 9 camera streams render at a fluid 30 frames per second (fps). HW3 Vehicles: The system throttles the Active Camera Preview display to 15 fps. This throttling is intentional. It preserves the vital processing cycles required for real-time risk mitigation. Additionally, HW3 vehicles do not possess the Front Bumper Camera, resulting in a 3-by-3 grid with one inactive tile. Despite these compromises, user feedback from the first wave of HW3 rollouts indicates that FSD v14 Lite exhibits exceptional stability. Lane-centering has been noticeably smoothed, and the annoying "camera degradation" alerts historically common during night driving have been substantially reduced due to upgraded noise-reduction algorithms integrated into the v14 vision pipeline. IV. Practical Real-World Use Cases for Daily Drivers Having an active nine-camera matrix on your dashboard is far more than a visual novelty. For Tesla owners in both North America and Europe, this feature resolves several long-standing daily driving pain points. 1. Enhanced Cabin & Passenger Monitoring For parents traveling with young children, infants, or pets in the rear seats, the Interior Cabin Camera is now a powerful tool. Instead of relying on physical back-seat mirrors (which are often poorly aligned and can degrade night-time visibility), drivers can keep a dedicated, high-contrast infrared feed of the back seat active on the right side of the screen. Because the cabin camera utilizes invisible infrared emitters, it provides crystal-clear visibility even during zero-light highway drives. 2. Low-Visibility Blind Spot Audits Although Tesla’s standard blind-spot camera feature activates a feed when turning on your turn signal, it only displays a single side view. With FSD v14.3.5 Active Preview, a driver merging into complex multi-lane highway systems can continuously view both B-pillar and side repeater feeds simultaneously. This is exceptionally helpful when navigating narrow European roundabouts or during heavy rains where water droplets on side windows distort physical side-mirror views. 3. Precision Towing and Hitching Alignment For Model Y or Cybertruck owners towing small campers, utility trailers, or bike racks, the rear-view camera and bumper camera feeds can now remain persistently on. This allows drivers to monitor hitch security, trailer sway, or loose cargo ties in real-time at full highway speeds, without having to shift into reverse to force-trigger the camera. 4. Curbside Guarding Navigating tight parallel parking spaces in congested European cities like Paris, Munich, or London often results in "curb rash" on expensive alloy wheels. By expanding the side-repeater views or the new front bumper camera (on equipped models) during tight maneuvers, drivers can visually verify their distance from stone curbs with millimeter precision, supplementing the ultrasonic or Tesla Vision distance warnings. V. Impact on Autonomous Driving Perception & Trust From a psychological perspective, Tesla’s decision to unlock these raw video feeds while in motion represents a significant shift in corporate philosophy. Historically, Tesla restricted access to these cameras to prevent driver distraction and mitigate legal liabilities. Demystifying "Phantom Braking" By offering real-time visibility, Tesla is building transparency with its user base. When FSD performs a sudden, unexpected speed reduction (popularly known as "phantom braking"), or shifts slightly in its lane, a driver can now immediately look at the active camera grid to see exactly what the car's computer saw. If a B-pillar camera was temporarily blinded by direct, low-angle sunlight, or if the wide front camera caught a flickering shadow from an overpass, the visual feedback helps the driver understand the system's "thought process." Regulatory Alignment The opening of these feeds also signals Tesla’s confidence in its hardware’s visual fidelity. European regulators (under the UNECE framework) have historically expressed skepticism regarding pure-vision autonomous systems. Providing drivers and potential regulatory auditors with direct, low-latency access to the vehicle's optical inputs helps demystify Tesla Vision's reliability in dense, complex European driving environments. Conclusion FSD v14.3.5 (2026.20.6.6) proves that Tesla is committed to refining both the functional capability of its autonomous driving suite and the qualitative user experience of the human inside. The Active Camera Preview is a massive leap forward in trust, safety, and operational utility. While HW3 owners must navigate the hardware limitations of a legacy processing platform, the software optimizations of the MLIR compiler ensure that every Tesla owner continues to benefit from the absolute cutting edge of automotive artificial intelligence. FAQ Q: Can I use Active Camera Preview if I do not have FSD (Supervised)? A: Yes. While the feature is bundled with FSD v14.3.5 updates, the Camera Preview function can be activated under the Service menu on any Tesla running the 2026.20.6.6 firmware, regardless of whether you have active FSD or basic Autopilot. Q: Does running the active 9-box grid drain more battery? A: The battery drain is negligible. The rendering is handled by the infotainment processor’s GPU, which operates on milliwatts of power relative to the high-voltage traction battery powering the motors. Q: Can I record these live previews directly to my USB drive? A: The Dashcam and Sentry Mode systems continue to record their standard designated channels in the background. The Active Camera Preview UI does not modify how files are written to your USB drive; it is purely a real-time monitor. Q: Is the interior cabin camera feed secure? Does Tesla upload this video? A: No. The live stream of the cabin camera displayed on your touchscreen is processed entirely locally on the car's computer and is not transmitted to Tesla's cloud servers, respecting occupant privacy. Q: Does the 9-box grid disappear automatically if I shift gears? A: Unlike previous software versions, where shifting into drive immediately killed the camera preview, the grid in 2026.20.6.6 remains persistent until you manually close it by tapping the "X" icon or swipe it away, regardless of your gear or driving state.

title: Vericel to Report Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results on July 30, 2026

body_text: Investor Relations Press Releases Vericel to Report Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results on July 30, 2026 July 16, 2026 at 8:30 AM EDT PDF Version BURLINGTON, Mass., July 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vericel Corporation (NASDAQ:VCEL), a leader in advanced therapies for the sports medicine and severe burn care markets, today announced that the Company will report its second quarter 2026 financial results on Thursday, July 30, 2026. Vericel’s management will host a conference call and webcast at 8:30 a.m. ET to discuss its financial results and business highlights. The live webcast can be accessed on the Investor Relations section of the Vericel website at http://investors.vcel.com/events-presentations . Presentation slides for the conference call will be available on the webcast and on the website. A replay of the webcast will be available until July 30, 2027. To participate by telephone, dial 800-330-6730 or +1-312-471-1351 if connecting from outside the U.S. When connected, please use passcode: 567253. About Vericel Corporation Vericel is a leading provider of advanced therapies for the sports medicine and severe burn care markets. The Company combines innovations in biology with medical technologies, resulting in a highly differentiated portfolio of innovative cell therapies and specialty biologics that repair injuries and restore lives. Vericel markets three products in the United States. MACI® (autologous cultured chondrocytes on porcine collagen membrane) is an autologous cellularized scaffold product indicated for the repair of symptomatic, single or multiple full-thickness cartilage defects of the knee with or without bone involvement in adults. Epicel® (cultured epidermal autografts) is a permanent skin replacement for the treatment of patients with deep dermal or full thickness burns greater than or equal to 30% of total body surface area. Vericel also holds an exclusive license for North American rights to NexoBrid® (anacaulase-bcdb), a biological orphan product containing proteolytic enzymes, which is indicated for eschar removal in adults and pediatric patients with deep partial-thickness and/or full-thickness burns. title: Good vs Bad LinkedIn Photos: What the Data Actually Reveals
summary: We analyzed thousands of LinkedIn profile photos to identify the best and worst trends, as well as what makes a headshot get more clicks.
body_text: Key Takeaways LinkedIn profiles with a professional photo receive up to 21x more profile views and 36x more messages than profiles without one Snappr analyzed tens of thousands of LinkedIn profile photos using its Photo Analyzer tool, making it the largest study of LinkedIn photo quality ever conducted. Law, consulting, and investment banking professionals consistently have the highest-quality LinkedIn headshots. Professionals with larger networks tend to have better profile pictures, suggesting photo quality and networking success reinforce each other. Senior employees counterintuitively tend to have worse photos than newer hires, likely because they haven't updated them in years. The hallmarks of a good LinkedIn profile picture: natural lighting, a clean background, industry-appropriate attire, and a genuine expression Update your LinkedIn photo every 1–2 years or after any significant change in appearance. Why Your LinkedIn Profile Picture Matters More Than You Think Your LinkedIn profile picture is the first thing people see when they find you on the platform, and it’s doing more work than most professionals realize. ‍ According to LinkedIn’s own data, profiles with a photo receive 21 times more views and up to 36 times more messages than profiles without one. That’s not a subtle difference. It’s the gap between being visible and invisible on the largest professional network in the world. ‍ But having any photo isn’t enough. Research in Psychological Science found that people form judgments about trustworthiness and competence from a face in as little as 100 milliseconds. Your LinkedIn headshot is being evaluated before a recruiter reads your headline, before a potential client checks your experience, and long before anyone clicks through to your full profile. ‍ The question isn’t whether your LinkedIn profile picture matters. It’s whether yours is helping or hurting you. ‍ That’s why we built the Snappr Photo Analyzer , a free tool that scores your LinkedIn profile picture and gives you specific feedback on how to improve it. Tens of thousands of professionals have used it, and the data they generated powers the largest analysis of LinkedIn photo quality ever undertaken. ‍ Here’s what we found. Good vs Bad LinkedIn Photos: What Our Data Shows We analyzed tens of thousands of Photo Analyzer results alongside anonymized data from the LinkedIn profiles they’re attached to. The goal was straightforward: identify the patterns that separate good LinkedIn profile pictures from bad ones, and understand what drives photo quality across geographies, industries, and career stages. Which Countries Have the Best LinkedIn Profile Pictures? Chile leads the world in LinkedIn photo quality, with Latin American and English-speaking countries dominating the top five. When we mapped Photo Analyzer scores by country, one result stood out: Chile ranks highest for LinkedIn photo quality, followed closely by several other Latin American and European nations. ‍ LinkedIn photo quality by country, based on tens of thousands of Snappr Photo Analyzer results. ‍ The pattern suggests that cultural norms around professional presentation vary significantly across regions. In countries where professional headshots are a standard part of career development, the average quality tends to be higher across the board. ‍ North American and Western European profiles scored solidly but showed wider variance. The best photos are excellent, but there’s a longer tail of low-quality images pulling the averages down. ‍ Which Industries Score the Highest? Law, chemicals, and nonprofit management lead the pack, while photography professionals ironically score lowest. Industry had one of the strongest correlations with photo quality in our dataset. The top-performing sectors were: Law Consulting Investment Banking Broadcast Media Staffing and Recruiting ‍ The common thread? These are industries where personal presentation is directly tied to credibility and client trust. A lawyer’s headshot isn’t vanity; it’s a professional tool. The same applies to consultants pitching new clients and recruiters whose profiles serve as their storefronts. ‍ Industries with lower scores tended to be those where professionals are less client-facing or where informal culture is the norm. However, this is changing rapidly as remote work makes your LinkedIn headshot your most common first impression. Does Your Network Size Affect Your Photo Quality? People with more LinkedIn connections tend to have higher-quality profile photos. Our data shows a clear correlation: people with larger LinkedIn networks tend to have higher-quality profile photos. The relationship is steady and consistent as connection counts increase. ‍ The likely explanation is bidirectional. Professionals who invest in their LinkedIn presence (including their photo) tend to be more active networkers. And a strong professional headshot may itself drive more connection requests, creating a virtuous cycle. ‍ Either way, if you’re trying to grow your network, your profile picture is one of the best places to start. The Seniority Paradox The longer someone stays in a role, the more likely their LinkedIn photo is outdated. Here’s the most counterintuitive finding in our data: people with more seniority in their current positions actually have worse LinkedIn photos, on average, than newer employees. ‍ Why? The most likely explanation is simple: they uploaded their photo years ago and haven’t updated it since. A VP who’s been in their role for eight years is probably still using the headshot they took when they were promoted. Meanwhile, someone who just started a new job is more likely to have refreshed their entire profile, photo included. ‍ It’s a reminder that your LinkedIn profile picture has a shelf life. What looked current in 2019 reads as dated today. What Makes a Good LinkedIn Profile Picture Based on our data and the patterns we’ve observed across tens of thousands of LinkedIn profile photos, here are the elements that consistently separate good LinkedIn headshots from bad ones. Lighting Natural, diffused light is the single biggest factor in LinkedIn photo quality. The best LinkedIn headshots use soft, even lighting that eliminates harsh shadows across the face. Indoor photos taken near a large window on an overcast day consistently score highest in our Photo Analyzer. ‍ Avoid overhead fluorescent lighting (it creates unflattering shadows under the eyes) and direct flash (it flattens features and creates a washed-out look). If you’re shooting outdoors, open shade (under a tree or next to a building) gives you the soft, even light that professional photographers look for. Background A clean, uncluttered background keeps the focus on you. The most effective LinkedIn profile picture backgrounds are: Solid neutral colors: grey, white, or muted blue Softly blurred office or outdoor environments Simple architectural settings with minimal distraction ‍ Avoid busy backgrounds with visible clutter, other people, or anything that competes with your face for attention. The best LinkedIn headshot backgrounds communicate professionalism without shouting. Framing and Composition Your LinkedIn photo should show your head and the tops of your shoulders, centered in the frame. This is the classic headshot composition, and it works because LinkedIn displays profile photos as small circles. Too much body and your face gets lost at that scale. ‍ Fill approximately 60–70% of the frame with your face and shoulders. Leave a small amount of space above your head. And make sure you’re looking directly at the camera. Eye contact matters even in a photograph. Expression and Body Language A slight, natural smile consistently outperforms both a neutral expression and a full grin. The goal is to look approachable and confident, not stiff or overly casual. ‍ The best approach: think about something that genuinely makes you happy right before the photo is taken. Forced smiles read as exactly that. A slight head tilt (around 10–15 degrees) can also add warmth without sacrificing professionalism. A dark suit and a clean white backdrop are a reliable combination for a professional LinkedIn headshot. What to Wear for a LinkedIn Photo Your attire should match the norms of your industry, but lean slightly more polished than your everyday work clothes. Finance, law, consulting: A well-fitted suit or blazer in a solid, dark color Tech, design, startups: A clean button-down, well-fitted sweater, or smart casual top Healthcare: A white coat or professional business attire Creative industries: More latitude, but keep it intentional. Your outfit should look chosen, not accidental ‍ Solid colors photograph better than busy patterns. Avoid logos, graphic tees, and anything with thin stripes (they create a moiré effect on camera). A simple neckline that frames your face works best. Bad LinkedIn Profile Examples: Common Mistakes to Avoid Some LinkedIn photo mistakes are obvious. Others are subtler but equally damaging to your professional image. Here are the most common patterns we see in low-scoring profiles: The group-photo crop. Cropping yourself out of a group photo always looks like exactly what it is. You’ll end up with someone else’s arm in the frame, an awkward off-center composition, and a blurry, low-resolution image. The vacation selfie. A selfie taken at the beach, at a bar, or at a wedding sends one clear message: you didn’t think your LinkedIn profile was worth a dedicated photo. Even a well-lit selfie struggles with the close-range distortion that wide-angle phone cameras create. The decade-old headshot. If you look noticeably different from your LinkedIn photo, you’re setting up every first meeting for an awkward moment of non-recognition. Your profile picture should look like you right now. No photo at all. The default grey silhouette is the worst-performing option by every metric LinkedIn tracks. Profiles without photos receive dramatically fewer views, connection requests, and messages. It’s the single most impactful change you can make to your profile. The overly casual shot. Sunglasses, hats, pets, and party settings may show personality, but they undermine credibility in a professional context. Save those for your personal social media. The over-edited portrait. Heavy filters, excessive retouching, and obviously artificial backgrounds can look polished at first glance but feel uncanny on closer inspection. Authenticity scores better than perfection. ‍ LinkedIn Headshot Tips by Industry Different industries have different expectations for professional headshots. Here’s how to calibrate your LinkedIn photo to your field. Finance and Law. These are the industries that consistently score highest in our Photo Analyzer data, and there’s a reason: professional headshots are treated as essential tools. Expect a dark blazer or suit, a solid background, and traditional studio lighting. Conservative but polished. Technology and Startups. The tech industry runs more casual, and your LinkedIn headshot can reflect that, but casual doesn’t mean careless. A clean shirt, good lighting, and a simple background still matter. You just have more latitude with color and setting. Healthcare. A white coat signals authority and expertise. If you’re a physician, it’s a strong choice for your profile picture. For administrators and non-clinical roles, standard business professional attire works well. Creative and Media. This is where you have the most room to express personality through your headshot. More creative compositions, interesting backgrounds, and distinctive styling can work, as long as your face is still clearly visible and the image reads as intentional. Sales and Recruiting. Your headshot is your storefront. Warmth and approachability matter more here than in most fields. A genuine smile, slightly warmer lighting, and a composition that feels inviting can directly impact your response rates. Taking a LinkedIn photo with your phone’s portrait mode can produce strong results if the lighting is right. How to Take a Good LinkedIn Photo With Your Phone You don’t necessarily need a professional photographer to get a strong LinkedIn profile picture. Modern smartphone cameras are more than capable if you set up the shot correctly. Use the rear camera, not the selfie camera. The rear camera on your phone has a significantly better lens with less distortion. Set a timer or ask someone to take the photo for you. Find your light. Stand facing a large window with indirect light. The light should be in front of you, not behind you. Avoid direct sunlight, which creates harsh shadows. Set up a clean background. A blank wall, a simple bookshelf, or a solid-color backdrop all work. Remove any clutter from the frame before shooting. Get the right distance. Have the photographer stand 4–6 feet away and zoom in slightly (1.5–2x) rather than shooting at the widest angle. This reduces the lens distortion that makes phone photos look like selfies. Take a lot of shots. Professional photographers typically shoot hundreds of images to get a handful of great ones. Take at least 50 photos with slight variations in expression and angle, then pick the best one. Edit lightly. Adjust brightness, contrast, and warmth. Crop to a headshot composition. Skip the heavy filters. You want a photo that looks like a better version of you, not a different person. ‍ Should You Use AI-Generated LinkedIn Headshots? AI headshot generators have become increasingly popular, offering studio-quality portraits without a camera. They’re fast, inexpensive, and convenient. But should you use one for your LinkedIn profile picture? ‍ The case for AI headshots: They produce consistent, well-lit, professional-looking results at a fraction of the cost of a traditional photo session. For professionals who work remotely and don’t have easy access to a studio, they can fill a gap. ‍ The case against: AI-generated photos can fall into the uncanny valley. They look almost right, but subtle issues with skin texture, lighting consistency, or eye reflections give them away. They’re also becoming easier to spot as more people encounter them. If someone realizes your headshot is AI-generated, it can undermine the authenticity you’re trying to project. ‍ The verdict: AI headshots are a reasonable interim solution — better than no photo or a bad photo. But for professionals in client-facing roles, leadership positions, or industries where trust and credibility are paramount, a real photo taken by a real photographer still carries more weight. A professional headshot captures something an algorithm can’t quite replicate: the way you actually look when you’re at your most confident and present. How Often Should You Update Your LinkedIn Photo? There’s no hard rule, but a reliable guideline is to update your LinkedIn profile picture every one to two years. You should also update it immediately if: You’ve changed your hairstyle or hair color significantly You’ve gained or lost a noticeable amount of weight You’ve changed industries or roles, and your current photo no longer matches the professional context Your photo is more than three years old You look at your profile and don’t quite recognize yourself ‍ Remember the seniority paradox from our data: tenured professionals tend to have worse photos specifically because they haven’t updated them. Don’t let inertia work against you. A quick refresh of your headshot takes less time than most meetings and has a longer-lasting impact on your career visibility. How to Get a Professional LinkedIn Headshot That Delivers Results If our data makes one thing clear, it’s that the quality of your LinkedIn profile picture directly correlates with professional outcomes: more profile views, more connection requests, and more messages from recruiters and potential clients. ‍ While DIY phone photos can get the job done in a pinch, there’s a noticeable quality gap between a self-shot photo and one taken by an experienced portrait photographer who understands how to work with lighting, angles, and composition to bring out your best. ‍ Snappr connects you with professional photographers in over 200 cities, with sessions that typically take 15–30 minutes and deliver polished, ready-to-use headshots within 48 hours. You can book a portrait session in under 60 seconds. ‍ For companies looking to upgrade their team’s LinkedIn presence at scale, whether it’s a leadership team, a sales organization, or an entire distributed workforce, Snappr’s enterprise photography solutions handle everything from scheduling across multiple locations to maintaining brand consistency across hundreds of headshots. ‍ And if you want to see where your current photo stands before booking anything, try the free Snappr Photo Analyzer. It takes seconds and gives you a data-backed score along with specific suggestions for improvement. Frequently Asked Questions What Is the Ideal Size for a LinkedIn Profile Picture? LinkedIn recommends a profile photo between 400 x 400 pixels and 7,680 x 4,320 pixels. The image displays as a circle, so make sure your face is centered, and nothing important is near the edges. A square crop at 800 x 800 pixels is a reliable standard. Should My LinkedIn Photo Be in Color or Black and White? Color is the standard and generally recommended. While black-and-white photos can look striking, they can feel dated or overly artistic for a professional networking platform. If you do choose black and white, make sure the contrast is strong, and your face reads clearly at a small size. Can I Use a Casual Photo on LinkedIn? It depends on your industry. In creative fields, tech startups, or roles where personality is valued, a slightly more casual LinkedIn headshot can work, as long as it’s still well-lit, well-composed, and intentional. In more traditional industries like finance, law, or healthcare, stick with a conventional professional headshot. Is It Worth Hiring a Photographer for LinkedIn Photos? The data suggests yes. Professional headshots consistently score higher across every metric we track, and the investment is modest compared to the career impact of a strong LinkedIn presence. A single session typically costs less than a business lunch, and the photos last several years. What Background Works Best for a LinkedIn Headshot? Neutral, solid-color backgrounds in grey, white, or muted blue consistently score highest in our Photo Analyzer. Softly blurred office or outdoor environments also perform well. The key principle is keeping the viewer’s focus on your face, not on what’s behind you. Is It Okay to Use a Graduation Photo on LinkedIn? A graduation photo can work for recent graduates entering the job market. It signals achievement and is usually taken professionally. However, once you’ve been in the workforce for more than a year or two, it’s time to update to a headshot that reflects your current professional identity.

title: 10 alimentos prohibidos para gatos que debes conocer urgente
summary: Cebolla, chocolate, uvas y más: los 10 alimentos tóxicos para gatos que nunca debes darles. Guía de emergencias y qué hacer si los ingirió.
body_text: Los gatos son animales curiosos que pueden acercarse a lo que comemos con aparente interés. Pero lo que es inofensivo o incluso saludable para los humanos puede ser extremadamente tóxico para ellos. En Colombia, donde la cultura de compartir comida con las mascotas es común, es fundamental que todos los tutores conozcan esta lista. Algunos de estos alimentos pueden causar falla orgánica y muerte en pocas horas. Emergencia veterinaria Si crees que tu gato ingirió alguno de estos alimentos, no esperes a que aparezcan síntomas. Llama inmediatamente a tu veterinario o acude a una clínica de urgencias. En Bogotá puedes contactar la Línea 311 de la Secretaría de Salud o clínicas veterinarias de urgencias 24 horas como Clínica Veterinaria Bogotá o Animal Center. Los 10 alimentos más peligrosos para tu gato 1. Cebolla y ajo (familia Allium) Este es probablemente el peligro más subestimado porque está presente en casi todas las comidas colombianas: el hogao, los guisos, las sopas. La cebolla y el ajo contienen compuestos organosulfurados (N-propil disulfuro) que destruyen los glóbulos rojos del gato causando anemia hemolítica. El daño es acumulativo: pequeñas cantidades repetidas son tan peligrosas como una dosis grande. El ajo es hasta 5 veces más tóxico que la cebolla. El puerro, la cebolleta y el cebollín también son peligrosos. 2. Chocolate y cacao El chocolate contiene teobromina y cafeína, dos estimulantes que los gatos no pueden metabolizar eficientemente. El chocolate negro y el cacao en polvo son los más peligrosos. Los síntomas incluyen vómito, diarrea, taquicardia, temblores, convulsiones y en casos severos, muerte. Incluso pequeñas cantidades de chocolate negro pueden ser letales para un gato de talla media. 3. Uvas y pasas Aunque el mecanismo exacto aún no se comprende completamente, se sabe que las uvas y las pasas causan falla renal aguda en gatos (y perros). Lo alarmante es que la toxicidad no parece depender de la dosis: incluso una sola uva puede desencadenar insuficiencia renal en algunos animales. Las uvas son muy consumidas en Colombia como snack; mantenlas fuera de su alcance. 4. Aguacate El aguacate contiene una toxina llamada persina que puede causar vómito, diarrea y dificultad respiratoria en gatos. En Colombia, donde el aguacate hass es de consumo diario, es importante no dejar cáscaras ni semillas al alcance del gato. La pulpa también es problemática, especialmente el hueso, que además representa un riesgo de obstrucción. 5. Masa cruda y levadura Si horneas en casa, nunca dejes masa cruda al alcance de tu gato. La levadura activa en la masa continúa fermentando en el estómago del gato, produciendo dióxido de carbono (causando distensión abdominal dolorosa) y alcohol etílico como subproducto. Esto puede causar desde distensión y dolor intenso hasta intoxicación alcohólica severa. 6. Xilitol (edulcorante artificial) El xilitol está presente en muchos productos "sin azúcar": chicles, caramelos, algunos yogures, pastas de dientes y suplementos. En los gatos provoca una liberación masiva de insulina que lleva a hipoglucemia severa (azúcar en sangre peligrosamente baja), y también puede causar daño hepático agudo. Lee siempre los ingredientes de los productos antes de que tu gato los alcance. 7. Alcohol Aunque parece obvio, el alcohol en cualquier forma (bebidas, alimentos fermentados, ciertos medicamentos) es extremadamente tóxico para los gatos. Su hígado no puede metabolizarlo y los efectos son similares a los de un humano, pero con dosis 10 veces más pequeñas. Incluso una cucharadita de whisky puede causar coma y muerte en un gato adulto. 8. Cafeína (café, té, bebidas energizantes) La cafeína es un estimulante del sistema nervioso central que puede causar en los gatos: hiperactividad, temblores, convulsiones, taquicardia, hipertensión y en dosis altas, la muerte. En Colombia el café es ubicuo, y los gatos pueden mostrar interés por las tazas abandonadas. No hay antídoto: el tratamiento es solo de soporte. 9. Macadamia y nueces Las nueces de macadamia son tóxicas para los felinos y caninos, causando debilidad muscular, temblores, fiebre y vómito. Otras nueces grandes como las nueces de nogal también pueden ser problemáticas por su contenido graso y la posibilidad de contener mohos productores de micotoxinas. En Colombia se usan mucho en repostería navideña: ten cuidado durante las fiestas. 10. Leche y derivados lácteos (en exceso) Aunque no es técnicamente "tóxico" como los anteriores, vale la pena mencionarlo porque el mito del gato que bebe leche está muy arraigado. La mayoría de los gatos adultos son intolerantes a la lactosa: les falta la enzima lactasa para digerirla bien. El resultado son diarreas, gases y malestar gastrointestinal. La leche para mascotas (sin lactosa) es una alternativa si quieres darles algo especial. Síntomas de intoxicación en gatos Los síntomas varían según el tóxico ingerido, pero las señales de alarma generales incluyen: Vómito repetido o espuma en la boca Diarrea, especialmente con sangre Letargia extrema o debilidad súbita Convulsiones o temblores Dificultad para respirar o respiración acelerada Pupilas dilatadas o contraídas de forma anormal Pérdida de coordinación o tambaleo al caminar Ictericia (coloración amarilla en encías o ojos) Orina muy oscura o ausencia de orina Qué hacer ante una intoxicación: pasos inmediatos 1. Mantén la calma. 2. Identifica qué ingirió y en qué cantidad aproximada. 3. No induzcas el vómito sin indicación veterinaria (puede empeorar algunos casos). 4. Lleva el empaque o una muestra del alimento al veterinario. 5. Ve a urgencias veterinarias lo antes posible, no esperes a que empeoren los síntomas. Snacks seguros y saludables para tu gato La buena noticia es que sí existen opciones seguras para darle algo especial a tu felino de vez en cuando: Permitidos con moderación Snacks seguros para gatos Pollo o pavo cocido (sin huesos, sin sal, sin condimentos) Atún o sardinas en agua (ocasionalmente, no como base de dieta) Zanahoria cocida en pequeñas cantidades Pepino fresco (hidratante y bajo en calorías) Snacks comerciales específicos para gatos disponibles en LAIKA Pasto gatuno (cat grass) cultivado en casa La regla de oro es sencilla: si tienes duda sobre si algo es seguro para tu gato, no lo des. Consulta siempre a tu veterinario antes de introducir cualquier alimento nuevo fuera de su dieta habitual. Los snacks comerciales de calidad diseñados específicamente para gatos son siempre la opción más segura. title: Silvercrest Asset Management Rebrands International and Global Value Platform as the Silvercrest Focused Value Platform
body_text: Silvercrest Asset Management Rebrands International and Global Value Platform as the Silvercrest Focused Value Platform July 23, 2026 10:30am EDT Download as PDF NEW YORK, July 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Silvercrest Asset Management Group Inc. (NASDAQ: SAMG) is pleased to announce that it has renamed its San Diego-based international and global value strategies as the Silvercrest Focused Value Platform . The new name reflects the philosophical and portfolio construction characteristics that distinguish the team’s investment approach. Managed by a highly experienced team of investment professionals, the Silvercrest Focused Value Platform offers concentrated Global, International, Emerging Markets, and International Small Cap strategies to institutional investors and select ultra-high-net-worth families and individuals. The strategies share defining characteristics—high conviction and concentration—setting the portfolios apart from other value managers. “This rebranding gives our clients a clearer picture of what has always set this team apart: a disciplined, concentrated, high-conviction approach to value investing across global markets. The Focused Value name draws that thread together,” said Allen Gray, Global Head of Institutional Business for Silvercrest. The rebranding does not change the team, its investment process, or the strategies themselves. It aligns the platform’s name with the way the team has always invested: building focused, high-conviction portfolios drawn from the full opportunity set across international and global markets. The Silvercrest Focused Value Platform operates independently from the Silvercrest Value Opportunity Platform, which draws on the full breadth of the value spectrum to generate alpha while targeting lower-volatility outcomes. Together, the two platforms give clients two genuinely distinct ways to access the alpha potential in value equities. About Silvercrest Silvercrest Asset Management Group LLC (the “firm”) is the principal operating subsidiary of Silvercrest Asset Management Group Inc. Silvercrest was founded in April 2002 as an independent, employee-owned registered investment adviser, headquartered in New York. The firm has seven additional offices in the United States, an office in Singapore, and team members based in Europe and Australia. As of March 31, 2026, the firm reported discretionary assets under management of $23.1 billion. Contact: Richard Hough 212-649-0601 rhough@silvercrestgroup.com Source: Silvercrest Asset Management Group Inc. Released July 23, 2026

title: German American Bank Awards $55,000 in Funds to Rauch, Inc. Through FHLBank Indianapolis Grant Program
body_text: German American Bank, a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank of Indianapolis (FHLBank Indianapolis), awarded Rauch, Inc. $55,000 in grant funds through the Community Multiplier – Member Match Program. The $55,000 grant will support Rauch’s housing department as they continue to grow and develop community-based, affordable, accessible housing in Clark, Floyd, and Scott counties. The funds will allow the organization to hire a part time Properties Coordinator to maintain the excellent level of service for current residents, freeing up time for the Director to concentrate on research, planning, and development of new housing projects. In addition, it will help to fund essential training for all employees. “German American Bank is proud to have a long-standing community partner in Rauch, Inc.,” says Brett Stilwell, German American Bank Market President. “We were excited to help them access funds from the Community Multiplier Grant to continue building their affordable housing program and support their mission to create a community where everyone belongs.” “The support of our community is what has allowed our organization to grow and thrive over the past 75 years,” states Dan Lowe, CEO of Rauch, Inc. “German American Bank and their willingness to step up make this grant a reality for us is a perfect example of that community support in action. We are so appreciative of their help.” The Community Multiplier – Member Match program is FHLBank Indianapolis’ newest program offering, designed to support targeted affordable housing initiatives that fall outside of FHLBank Indianapolis’ other grant programs. Community Multiplier offers grants between $25,000 and $125,000 for non-profit organizations headquartered in Indiana or Michigan who partner with an FHLBank Indianapolis member financial institution on targeted affordable housing initiatives. With a 10% matching funds commitment from the member financial institution, FHLBank Indianapolis is providing grants between $25,000 and $125,000. Share Copy Email

title: Why Community Health Systems Need Right-Sized Healthcare Data Analytics Right Now
summary: Discover why right-sized, scalable data and analytics solutions like Ignite Spark™ are helping community health systems overcome challenges, unlock insights, and sustain care delivery. ...
body_text: Community health systems are under growing strain. Shrinking margins, heavier regulatory requirements, and persistent workforce shortages are eroding stability. With reimbursement rates for Medicare and Medicaid often falling short, many hospitals now struggle to keep even the most essential services open. Community Health Systems: The Overlooked Majority Representing 84% of U.S. hospitals , one-third of which are in rural areas, community health systems are the backbone of healthcare delivery. They serve as providers, economic engines, and lifelines for vulnerable populations. Yet, despite their essential role, they often operate with fewer resources and narrower margins while still delivering the same quality of care as larger, better-funded health systems. Challenges Unique to Community Health Systems Mid-market systems face the same industry-wide challenges as large health systems—but with unique constraints: Locked into Siloed Systems Many community health systems are confined to rigid electronic health record ecosystems, making it difficult to unify data across clinical, financial, and operational domains. Without effective healthcare data integration , these organizations struggle to generate the insights needed for performance improvement, strategic planning, and better patient care. Fragmented Vendor Ecosystems A patchwork of niche point solutions addresses individual needs but creates a fragmented technology landscape. This lack of alignment leads to data silos and a limited view of organizational performance. Enterprise Platforms Are Out of Reach Solutions designed for large-scale systems are often too expensive, too complex, and too resource-intensive for mid-sized operations to implement and maintain. Generic Tools Fall Short While industry-agnostic platforms offer flexibility, they place the burden of customization—like clinical data modeling, governance, and metrics —on teams that lack the bandwidth or expertise to do it well. Introducing Health Catalyst Ignite Spark™ Ignite Spark is a healthcare data and analytics solution built for community hospitals and regional practices. It breaks through traditional barriers—cost, complexity, and capacity—to give mid-market organizations the tools they need to unify information through healthcare data integration , make data-informed decisions, improve outcomes, and thrive in today’s healthcare landscape. Designed around the principle of “right-sized” analytics, Ignite Spark delivers the right level of capability, scalability, and support for community health systems. Rather than forcing smaller organizations into oversized enterprise tools or undersized generic platforms, it aligns analytics power with available resources— so teams can act on insights without overextending budgets, infrastructure, or staff. Ignite Spark is also foundational—it helps make sense of data across clinical, operational, and financial domains. Most organizations start with a focused need, such as regulatory reporting or cost improvement, and expand from there, making advanced insights attainable, sustainable, and impactful for community healthcare. Ignite Spark offers: • Unified Data, Not Silos Ignite Spark connects with existing EHRs and systems, bringing clinical, financial, and operational data together into one trusted source. • One Platform, Not a Patchwork Instead of juggling multiple niche vendors, Ignite Spark streamlines analytics in a single solution—lowering costs and reducing complexity. • Enterprise Power, Without the Enterprise Price Tag Ignite Spark delivers enterprise-grade analytics at a scale and cost that mid-market health systems can actually sustain. • Healthcare-Specific, Not Generic Pre-built healthcare models, metrics, and governance come standard, so teams don’t carry the burden of customization or lack of expertise. Partner for the Long Haul Health Catalyst has long been a trusted partner to large health networks. With Ignite Spark, mid-market systems gain a trusted guide to navigate complexity as they modernize data infrastructure, unlock insights, and drive measurable improvement. Are you ready to bring enterprise-grade power to your lean team? Learn More ‍
